AvailableAdvisors.Name: Merdred Igrus
AvailableAdvisors.Description: Merdred Igrus carries himself with the careful dignity of a man who has spent decades navigating the courts of great houses and knows precisely which words open which doors. He manages the baron's diplomatic correspondence, legal affairs, and courtly protocol with the same unhurried confidence — nothing escapes his attention, and no slight against the barony's honour goes unaddressed. His knowledge of feudal law and noble etiquette is encyclopedic, his network of contacts among neighbouring lords quietly enviable. He is, in short, exactly as indispensable as he believes himself to be.

AvailableAdvisors.Name: Sir Loren Birely
AvailableAdvisors.Description: Sir Loren Birely is a broad-shouldered, grey-templed veteran who has kept Darkhold's walls and streets safe through two decades of service without ever once needing to raise his voice twice. He commands the baron's household guard and city watch with the quiet authority of a man who has seen enough trouble to recognise it early, and enough loyalty to deal with it firmly. He is not a man given to pleasantries or lengthy reports — a nod means the walls are secure, a frown means someone will regret it by morning. The baron sleeps soundly in no small part because Sir Loren does not.

AvailableAdvisors.Name: Albus Durdwale
AvailableAdvisors.Description: Albus Durdwale is a small, slightly stooped man with ink-stained fingers and a permanent squint that suggests he has spent more of his life peering at ledgers than at the horizon — which is, in fact, entirely true. What he lacks in stature and constitution he makes up for in relentless thoroughness: every bushel of grain, every hired hand, and every cart leaving Darkhold is accounted for in his cramped but precise hand. He is not a man who inspires confidence at first glance, and he knows it, which perhaps explains the faint nervousness that follows him from the granary to the tax office and back. But the barony's logistics have not failed on his watch, and quietly, without fanfare, that is exactly the point.

Advisors.Title: Chancellor
Advisors.Description: One of the barony's most important offices. The chancellor manages the ruler's dealings with vassals and liege lords, reads the loyalty and mood of subjects toward the government, and works to shape both. The office also oversees cultural development. A chancellor may lead through affection—easing conflicts and appealing to reason—through fear, threats, and harsh penalties for disobedience, or through a balanced mix of both.

Advisors.Title: Guard Captain
Advisors.Description: Essential in the smallest realms: at once lawkeeper, military commander, and guardian of the baron and their lands. Later most of these duties pass to a general, border warden, chief judge, and others—but until the barony grows into a principality, the Guard Captain alone is enough to handle them.

Advisors.Title: Steward
Advisors.Description: The Steward oversees everything tied to income, construction, provisions, and tax collection.

BaronyRelations.Name: Millena Canterill
BaronyRelations.Title: Baronet
BaronyRelations.Description: After the death of the family's head — Rydan Canterill, known as the Goat — his widow took over his estate. As Rydan left four daughters and no son, it is women who now rule the house of the Brown Canterills. The old matron enjoys good relations with her distant cousin, Margrave Argewald, and so no one has yet attempted to push them off their lands. Baronet Millena jealously guards the virtue of her daughters, warning every suitor that in the event of a match he will be required to renounce his own family name. So far there has been no shortage of willing men, yet none has found favour with the fastidious matron. The Brown Canterills hold the southwestern lands, together with the village of Durbale, a manor house, and a defensive tower.

BaronyRelations.Name: Jochim Bullewyn
BaronyRelations.Title: Baronet
BaronyRelations.Description: A wealthy house by Darkhold's standards. The baronet is shrewd and cautious — a man of good sense and a nose for profit, though he has not been known to be overly corrupt or to abuse his position. The family originates from the central Empire and won their lands in Darkhold as a reward for service in the War of Kildrad. The house holds the village of Raven's Claw and the surrounding lands; the Bullewyn manor stands within it, though the family also maintains a residence in the town of Darkhold.

BaronyRelations.Name: Olgred Trur
BaronyRelations.Title: Viscount of Brie
BaronyRelations.Description: Of Kildrad blood. His father Omir yielded Brie to Hardwin Greatwing after a short siege in exchange for peace and no sack, then ruled cautiously for thirty years—loved by commoners, pressed by ambitious neighbours (including Darkhold under Thaddeus Direbolt’s predecessors). After Omir’s death Olgred raised taxes, hardened the law, seized debtors’ goods, enlarged the guard, retook land from vacant Darkhold, and made war on Baron Corlin Werdhog of Klin. Early gains collapsed when Werdhog hired the eastern sellsword company Scarlet Desire, who night-attacked Olgred, butchered half his guard, and drove him off. Raids continue. Vassal of Marquis Argewald Canterill of Totham; he pays his dues and keeps his wars within the law, so Argewald does not intervene.

BaronyRelations.Name: Arienna Coler
BaronyRelations.Title: Baroness of Thyruswill
BaronyRelations.Description: Widow of Lord Luden Canterill, who died childless and left her everything—to his house’s fury. Thyruswill stands on the Moonlake peninsula where Hardwin Greatwing once sacked and burned Moonhall after a bitter siege; Luden oversaw its rebuilding under Turderweld of the Canterills. Arienna, once Luden’s concubine and later his wife after Herdwig’s death, is a sharp politician who kept the barony despite Canterill lawsuits by winning Margrave Hardwin’s favour and breaking their embargo. Suitors flock; she plays them against each other and refuses to remarry. She pays the highest peace-fee (30%) and obeys her liege, yet Marquis Argewald Canterill still withholds the viscountess’s title.

BaronyRelations.Name: Dyron Greatwing
BaronyRelations.Title: Baron of Hurtbow
BaronyRelations.Description: Tall, thin, and little given to ambition—known for intelligence and a love of learning, logic, and games. Young nephew of Margrave Hardwin Greatwing, appointed to Hurtbow after decades of Dalish war on the Irredale fringe: Walch Hurtmere’s feud, peasant revolt for the Empire, failed hostage diplomacy, Lucius Greatwing’s death in ambush, and Urglim Mad Bull’s brutal campaigns that only deepened the hatred. After Urglim fell, neighbours—through Lord Erac Mertyn—bought a fragile peace with the Dalish for his body, goods, and an admission of defeat. Dyron’s arms split Greatwing with a green field and black lion; he is only beginning to settle into a hard, impoverished border barony.

BaronyRelations.Name: Durisug Dag'Thorak
BaronyRelations.Title: Marquis (Mountain Prince) of Groundfall
BaronyRelations.Description: Hard, unyielding dwarf lord of the Gray Mountains and the Venomous Pass—the only easy gate from the Salt Marshes into the March. Clan Dag'Thorak (Dagonite Shield) has held Groundfall for over seven centuries; they became Kildrad’s vassals in the Great Hunger in exchange for food and medicine, kept their own law, tongue, faith, and a tribute of dwarf-wrought arms, and later swore to Hardwin Greatwing on unchanged terms after he took three of Durisug’s sons hostage. Direct vassal of the Margrave: he pays tax and war-dues, yet keeps special rights for dwarves in the Eastern March. Without Groundfall’s fort, lizardfolk raiders and marsh-beasts would spill fifty miles inland.

BaronyRelations.Name: Turen Koltberg
BaronyRelations.Title: Baronet of Um
BaronyRelations.Description: One of three feuding Koltberg baronet-brothers in the barren Koltberg Hollow east of Darkhold—reached only by steep goblin-haunted paths through the Gray Mountains. Um is his village and chicken-coop “seat.” Officially a vassal of Marquis Argewald Canterill, who never collects tax or summons them to war: the hollow has no ores, little timber, and thin soil. The brothers—sons of Willis the Stout by different mothers—wage drunken “wars” with clubs and wormwood spirits, then lose interest before anything is decided. Little respected and usually ignored in March politics.

BaronyRelations.Name: Dunna Koltberg
BaronyRelations.Title: Baronet of Holdywag
BaronyRelations.Description: Koltberg baronet of Holdywag, third of the quarrelsome brothers of the hollow. Same poverty, same club-and-spirit “sieges,” same empty claim to rule the vale. March lords leave the Koltbergs alone until something worth taxing grows there—which never has.

BaronyRelations.Name: Will the Stammerer
BaronyRelations.Title: Baronet of Arg
BaronyRelations.Description: Koltberg baronet of Arg in the same poor hollow as Turen and Dunna. Claims the whole vale by blood; fights his half-brothers in farcical village brawls rather than true campaigns. House Koltberg is known for poverty, wildness, and inbreeding rumours—outstanding ears, mangy faces, hunched frames. Like his kin he is a vassal of Argewald Canterill in name only.
